title: Effect of Smoking and Time of Day on Eosinophils
official: Effects of Acute Smoking and Time of Day on Blood Eosinophils in Humans
summary: The study investigates the effect of acute smoking and time of day on blood eosinophils in chronic smokers. Chronic cigarette smokers without chronic respiratory diseases smoking at least 8 cigarettes per day and never-smoking controls are examined. Blood eosinophil counts and surface molecules are measured at 8 and 12 am in both groups. In smokers, two measurements are performed (at least 4 weeks apart): one measurement with no smoking between 8 and 12 am, and another measurement with smoking of 8 cigarettes between 8 and 12 am.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Healthy current smokers
* Age between 18-50 years
* Smoking of at least 8 cigarettes/day

Exclusion Criteria:

* Chronic respiratory diseases
* Any treatment with corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants
* Any acute illness
